source: docs/GOAL-2026-11-17-long-jobs.md section 1 (jobs L1 to L3, held-out H1 to H3, interruption steps I1 to I5); read by tools/job_run.py
notes: line: what the player types, one line, no hint of how. It is sent once at the trial's start; nothing else is sent.
end: the end predicate, read from the game by tools/job_run.done(). Every key must hold. Item patterns are fnmatch globs on item ids; '|' separates alternatives.

bar: Luis's per-unit times (data/baselines/luis-2026-11-01.json) composed into a floor for the job (tools/job_run.bar_s). null = no baseline covers the job; the verdict always uses quest_run.human_bar on the run's own successful steps (walking included), as quest runs do.

start: a checkpoint label (logs/quests/checkpoints) or a character save name that is forked for each trial (tools/quest_clone.fork; ClaudeDev.json is only read). interrupt_from: a mid-job checkpoint made by a real run (rule 8: trial --until first_step --save-as LABEL); while it does not exist, interruption trials start from 'start' and the interruption is put in after his first verified step.
not_carried_at_start: item patterns he must not hold when the trial starts; a trial that starts holding any is recorded and not counted (as quest_run's head start).

in_own_chest want 'gained': true: only what went into the container after the line counts (its count at the start: the harness's inspect before the line, else the body's read at his first store or take into it; neither read and enough inside: unread, never a pass).

world_needs: [{resource, match?, at_least, within_m, of ('home' = his my_bases base with the most pieces | 'start' | [x, y]), steps?}]: what the WORLD must hold for the job. Before the brain starts and the line is sent, tools/job_run.world_check counts the standing sources with the body's census (rows whose class, name, item or id holds match, within within_m in 2D, not available = false); short or unread, the line is never sent and the trial is recorded not counted ('world short: flax 14 of 22 within 350 m of home'), a fault of the run. A need holds for whole trials; for a step trial only with steps: true or a list naming the step.
deadline_s: the job's own per-trial deadline (default 1800); job_run --deadline wins.
interrupt_trigger: when an interruption trial puts the interruption in (tools/job_run.trigger_due); --trigger overrides it; default first_step.

work_tools: the tool calls that count as working the job (first verified step, and 'took the job up again' after an interruption). go_to is left out on purpose: after a death it may be the walk to the grave.

I4.how: fixture grant of a filler item to HIS bag only (the fork's guid; the fixture refuses while any other player is on), one unit per empty slot
I4.job_note: on N1 every unit he still needs merges into a stack he holds (stacks of 99) and a store needs no bag room: a full bag never meets a call of his (study 2026-11-18 i4_i5)
I4.long_note: 2026-11-20: I4 inside a long job (L1, L2 and its rung V1, L3), by the same dev-world fixture (his bag filled to the last slot with the filler). The gate is the job's own end (job_run.end_owed): an end item he does not hold yet that takes a new slot when he makes or picks it (made_carried, worn_made_in_run, gear_target; a chest want he carries none of); before any read, the trigger time alone. Give the trigger (--trigger at:SECONDS). The step's pass reads both: he took the job up again with no new line within resume_within_s (as N2) AND the job's end read from the game (verdict bar job_done), so the trial runs to the end (--until done, the default there). A rung or job whose end names no such item (V2 venture_gear, K, the held-out jobs, N1) is refused with the reason.
I4.from_note: a checkpoint pair saved by an N1 run with --until own_chest (job_run trial --confirm --job N1 -k 3 --until own_chest --save-as job_n1_own_chest): at home, a crate whose owner is HIM by the game holding some ash or stone, no redberries on him (rule 8: from a run, never hand-built). It was job_n1_done (a whole N1 run): the same problem as N1's steps, since a whole run's end counts ClaudeDev's crate as his line's (game_owner), so a done save can still have no crate of his own, and a fork of ClaudeDev for N2 meets the base crates 'ClaudeDev's, not mine' and asks which to use. Until it exists the window starts from N2's start (ClaudeDev: 5 stone, 1 ash, no redberries).
I4.note: Coarse Net: weight 1, a stack of 1, so N empty slots take N nets with little weight (a full bag, not an over-weight one). Unverified: whether one grant of N unstackable items fills N slots; job_run re-reads the empty slots and grants again up to 'rounds' times. between_calls: the grant waits until no call of his is open, so the bag is full before his next gather, not inside one. needs_new_slot: the grant waits until he carries none of an asked kind. The fill is full_read only: the step took when a call of his met the full bag (job_run.bag_watch: a result inventory_full, or a gather or pickup of the unheld kind that came back short), cleared at the first read with room after that, and he resumed when a call after the clear moved the job by the game's reads (job_run.serves_test). A full bag that met no call is not counted. The body's gather counts room on the hotbar and item page only (inventory.room_of, commit 6418592), so a refused pickup at room 0 ends inventory_full with what fills the bag. After each grant job_run waits up to settle_s (default 5 s) for his client's read to show it (job_run.settled_room), so a round never grants again on a stale read.

I5.how: the harness's own brain process (chat_ladder.start_brain) is ended (stop_brain: taskkill /T) and started again on the same world store (DW_WORLD_GUID); the body is not touched
I5.note: the open ask is on disk per world guid (brain/ask_store.py): job_run clears it at each trial's start (Live.clear_ask, no brain running) and keeps it across the restart inside the trial; the record says whether the new brain logged ask_restored (beside the verdict, not a bar). The record keeps the call open at the kill (moment.open_call), the stop, start and ready times apart, and at_clear: his bag and his containers read at ready. A job the in-flight call finished (at_clear done) is not counted (run 021010). He resumed only with a call after ready that moved the job by the game's reads (job_run.serves_test): upkeep and fuel do not count.
